channel.title: The Grant Desk - Grants, Remote & Worldwide, weekly digest
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: Grants, Remote & Worldwide, weekly digest. Released weekly: each Sunday's drop carries one entry per grant added in the week before it (Sunday to Saturday). A call that closes before its drop goes out is not sent; the website lists those.

item.title: Theatertreffen International Forum 2027, Berlin: 18-day scholarship for emerging theatre makers (all costs covered, no stipend) (closes 26 Nov)
item.description:
Berliner Festspiele, Theatertreffen, with the Goethe-Institut, Pro Helvetia and partners
Deadline: 26 Nov 2026, 23:59 CET
Award: NO CASH STIPEND; listed as a deliberate exception. The scholarship covers all participation costs: festival tickets, travel, Berlin public transport, shared accommodation, catering or a per diem, travel and health insurance and visa fees for those not resident in Berlin. No application fee mentioned.

Around 30 theatre makers at the start of their practice spend the whole of Theatertreffen 2027 in Berlin together: watching the invited productions, taking workshops with artists, joining artist talks and excursions, and meeting the festival director and jury.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Ocean Culture Life: Storytelling Grants 2027 (GBP 1,000, 3,000 or 5,000 for ocean stories in any medium) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Ocean Culture Life
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026
Award: Grants of GBP 1,000, GBP 3,000 and GBP 5,000; applicants choose the level that matches their production costs

Annual grants, now in their fourth year, for creators telling ocean stories in any medium: film, photography, writing, audio, illustration and art.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: 500 Capp Street: International Artist Exhibition Open Call 2026-2027 (closes 31 Dec)
item.description:
500 Capp Street (David Ireland House), with support from the Sanger Family Foundation
Deadline: 31 Dec 2026
Award: USD 5,000 artist honorarium, plus up to USD 10,000 toward production, fabrication, research, public programme and travel

Annual open call for one artist to develop an exhibition at 500 Capp Street, the historic San Francisco home and living sculpture of conceptual artist David Ireland. Open to individual artists in the United States and worldwide, with international artists especially encouraged.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: The Stringer Awards 2027: multi-year unrestricted cash awards for journalists and creative practitioners exposing abuses of power (aiming for USD 9,000-100,000) (closes 31 Dec)
item.description:
The Stringer Foundation
Deadline: 31 Dec 2026
Award: Multi-year, unrestricted cash awards; the foundation aims for grants between USD 9,000 and USD 100,000, depending on funds raised. No application fee mentioned.

The Stringer Foundation gives multi-year, unrestricted cash awards to people who use public media to expose abuses of power and injustices that harm the public, while upholding the truth.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Humboldt Residency Programme 2027, "Oceanic Horizons: The Future of our Blue Planet" (funded six-week residency for researchers, creatives and practitioners) (closes 14 Dec)
item.description:
Alexander von Humboldt Foundation
Deadline: 14 Dec 2026
Award: Monthly allowance for the six-week residency (figure not published: researchers get standard Humboldt fellowship rates, creatives and practitioners a competitive honorarium), travel allowance to and from Germany, accommodation at Schloss Wiepersdorf and a Berlin aparthotel, and a budget for public formats. No family allowance. No application fee.

Each year the Humboldt Foundation brings twelve people from research, the arts and civil society together to work on one topic and find new ways of communicating it to audiences beyond academia. The 2027 topic is Oceanic Horizons: The Future of our Blue Planet.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: ligeti zentrum Artists and Scientists in Residence 2027, Where Sound Shapes Space (Hamburg; EUR 1,200 a month plus accommodation) (closes 10 Jan 2027)
item.description:
ligeti zentrum (Hamburg University of Music and Theatre, HAW Hamburg and partners)
Deadline: 10 Jan 2027, 23:59 CET
Award: Scholarship of EUR 1,200 net per month for the residency, plus accommodation in Hamburg, a workspace, use of the Production Lab, basic technical support and professional documentation. Travel is not mentioned. No application fee mentioned.

Fifth round of the ligeti zentrum's artistic-scientific residency in Hamburg. Each resident joins one of four running projects on sound and space.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: MPI Short Film Lab 2027: narrative short film lab with fellowship grants and a USD 10,000 script grant (theme: For the Greater Good?) (closes 29 Nov)
item.description:
Moving Picture Institute (MPI)
Deadline: 29 Nov 2026, 23:59 PST
Award: Filmmakers accepted into the lab receive fellowship grants (amount not published). One official selection receives a USD 10,000 grant, which includes MPI acquiring the script for further development. Travel support for the Los Angeles summit is not mentioned. No application fee mentioned.

The Moving Picture Institute is a production company and talent incubator that makes films about human freedom. Its Short Film Lab takes writer-directors from a concept to a finished short script, and can lead to production as an MPI Original film. THEME 2027: For the Greater Good?

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Kinship: Nature Culture Fellowship 2027 (online; micro-grants of USD 1,000 to 2,000 for selected fellows) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Kinship
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026
Award: Micro-grants of USD 1,000 to 2,000 plus mentorship for selected fellows' community projects; not every fellow is funded

Global fellowship on culture, storytelling and ecological change for artists, storytellers, scientists, educators, community organisers, researchers and activists aged 18 and over.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: MOPGA 2027: Visiting Fellowship Program for Early Career Researchers (France) (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Campus France, for the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Space
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026
Award: EUR 2,500 a month for 12 months, plus a EUR 500 settling-in allowance and health, civil liability and repatriation insurance. International travel is not covered.

Tenth call of Make Our Planet Great Again, a French government visiting fellowship for early career researchers to spend 12 months in a French laboratory.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Epistemics Fund (sponsored by Ought, via Lightcone Commons): grants for tools that help people find what is true (USD 500,000 to 5 million pool) (closes 26 Nov)
item.description:
Ought, organised by Nathan Young on Lightcone Commons
Deadline: 26 Nov 2026
Award: Ought plans to make between USD 500,000 and USD 5 million in grants in total to the top-ranked applications (the page writes '$'; US dollars assumed). No fixed grant size: evaluators rank applications and funders decide how much each receives. Example asks on the page range from 150,000 to 1 million. No application fee.

A one-off fund for epistemics: tools and projects that help people work out what is true. AREAS: community notes (including AI note writers and rating tools); notes beyond social media (podcasts, papers, video, the open web); provenance tracking (C2PA support, reverse video search, synthetic-frame...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: The Aftermath Project: 2026 Post-Conflict Photography Grant (USD 25,000) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
The Aftermath Project
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026
Award: One USD 25,000 production grant (paid 50% at start, 40% midway, 10% on delivery); four additional finalists named. No application fee stated.

The Aftermath Project funds documentary photographers telling the other half of the story of conflict: what it takes for individuals, communities and nations to rebuild and heal after war.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: NLnet Foundation: Open Call January 2027 (Restack, CodeSupply and general fund) (closes 3 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Stichting NLnet (with European Commission backing; successor to the NGI Zero programme)
Deadline: 3 Jan 2027, 12:00 CET
Award: EUR 5,000 to 50,000 for a first grant, scalable in follow-ups; the Restack fund alone will award EUR 7 million through 2030. No application fee.

NLnet's January 2027 open call (deadline 3 January 2027, 12:00 CET; the proposal form may open shortly) funds open-source technical development: software and hardware released under free licenses.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: GLEAM 2027: Request for Light-Based Artwork Proposals (Olbrich Botanical Gardens; honorariums USD 5,000 to 30,000) (closes 6 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Olbrich Botanical Gardens (City of Madison Parks Division and Olbrich Botanical Society)
Deadline: 6 Jan 2027, 23:59 CST
Award: All-inclusive honorarium of USD 5,000 to 30,000 per artwork, covering artist fee, materials, fabrication, travel, lodging, install and maintenance. Usually only one USD 30,000 project is selected; proposals under USD 25,000 get the most consideration. Free host lodging and loan projectors and speakers are available. No application fee stated.

GLEAM is an annual night-time light art exhibition across a 16-acre botanical garden and a 10,000 sq ft tropical conservatory.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: The Whickers Film & TV Funding Award 2027 (GBP 120,000 for a first feature documentary) (closes 22 Jan 2027)
item.description:
The Whickers
Deadline: 22 Jan 2027, 12:00 GMT
Award: GBP 120,000 main award; GBP 25,000 development award for the runner-up. Free to enter.

The Whickers Film & TV Funding Award backs a director-led documentary by a first-time feature director. The winner receives GBP 120,000 and the runner-up a GBP 25,000 development award.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: IDFA Bertha Fund: IBF Classic 2027 (documentary development up to EUR 7,500, production up to EUR 25,000) (closes 10 Feb 2027)
item.description:
IDFA Bertha Fund (IDFA, Amsterdam)
Deadline: 10 Feb 2027
Award: Project Development up to EUR 7,500; Production and Post-production up to EUR 25,000. No application fee mentioned.

The IDFA Bertha Fund's IBF Classic scheme supports creative documentaries by filmmakers from countries on its Global South and Eastern Europe country list.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Iris Prize 2027: International LGBTQ+ Short Film Prize (GBP 40,000) (closes 2 Jun 2027)
item.description:
Iris Prize
Deadline: 2 Jun 2027
Award: GBP 40,000 for the winner to make their next short film in the UK; smaller UK-only awards (Community and Education GBP 250, Micro Short GBP 100). Submission fee not stated on the official page; Iris alumni get a full waiver.

Billed as the world's largest LGBTQ+ short film prize, the Iris Prize international shorts strand is open worldwide; the Best British, student, community and education strands are UK only. Submissions open 11 January 2027; deadlines: early bird 31 March, regular 24 May, late 2 June 2027.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Awesome Foundation Conservation and Climate Chapter: USD 1,000 Micro-grants (worldwide, rolling)
item.description:
Awesome Foundation (Conservation and Climate Chapter)
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: USD 1,000 per grant, no strings attached, paid via PayPal, Wise or Venmo. No application fee.

A volunteer-run, self-funded giving circle in the Awesome Foundation network that awards USD 1,000 micro-grants to innovative projects on wildlife conservation, habitat protection, climate change, ecotourism or environmental communication.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Awesome Foundation On the Water Chapter: USD 1,000 Monthly Micro-grants for Water-focused Projects (worldwide) (rolling)
item.description:
Awesome Foundation (On the Water Chapter)
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: USD 1,000 per month, one grant, no strings attached. No application fee.

An Awesome Foundation chapter run by artists and cultural producers that gives a USD 1,000 grant every month to a water-focused project that "adds awesome to the world".

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Perspective Fund: Documentary Film Support (production, post and impact grants) (rolling)
item.description:
Perspective Fund
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: Grants typically USD 25,000 to 150,000 per documentary and its impact campaign. No application fee stated.

Perspective Fund's Documentary Film Support programme gives grants, typically USD 25,000 to 150,000, to nonfiction documentaries driving social change and their engagement campaigns.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: IIE x OceanX Ocean Futures Fellowship 2027-28 (remote, monthly stipend; AI, immersive media and digital archives tracks) (closes 17 Nov)
item.description:
Institute of International Education (IIE) with OceanX
Deadline: 17 Nov 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: Monthly stipend (amount not published), plus a technology stipend for some fellows case by case. No application fee.

A 12-month remote fellowship from IIE and the ocean-exploration organisation OceanX for recent graduates using digital media, immersive storytelling and technology to connect ocean science with the public.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Cities Deliver: AI Solutions for Public Services (Rockefeller Foundation and OpenAI Foundation, USD 500,000 to 2 million) (closes 29 Nov)
item.description:
The Rockefeller Foundation and OpenAI Foundation, managed by RF Catalytic Capital (RFCC)
Deadline: 29 Nov 2026
Award: USD 50 million total. Seed track USD 500,000 to under 1 million; Scale track USD 1 to 2 million. 24-month grants, 50 percent at start and 50 percent on a documented mid-term milestone. No application fee stated.

A USD 50 million open call from the Rockefeller Foundation and OpenAI Foundation for organisations working with city governments to improve public services through AI, especially for underserved communities.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme 2027/28 (HKD 344,400 a year for up to three years; 400 fellowships, practice-led art PhDs included) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Research Grants Council (RGC) of Hong Kong, with eight Hong Kong universities
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 12:00 Hong Kong time
Award: Annual stipend of HKD 344,400 (about USD 44,150) plus a conference and research travel allowance of HKD 14,400 a year, for up to three years (2026/27 rates as published by the RGC). Some universities add top-ups: HKBU lists a HKD 40,000-a-year Elite Scholar Award for three years, a further HKD 20,000 travel top-up, four years of tuition waiver and two years of guaranteed accommodation. 400 fellowships for 2027/28.

The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme, run by the Research Grants Council, funds around 400 new full-time PhD students a year at eight Hong Kong universities, in any discipline, including AI, computing and data science programmes and practice-led art research (Hong Kong Baptist University's Academy...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: National Geographic Society: The Human Thread RFP (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
National Geographic Society (Center for Human Histories and Cultures, with support from Lilly Endowment Inc.)
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026
Award: Level I: up to US$20,000 (for applicants new to National Geographic funding, one year to implement). Level II: up to US$100,000 (for more established applicants, two years to implement).

Request for proposals from the National Geographic Society's Center for Human Histories and Cultures, funded by Lilly Endowment Inc.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: IHS AI and the Workforce Research Grants (up to USD 20,000) (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Institute for Humane Studies (IHS)
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026
Award: Up to USD 20,000 per award; larger awards possible for exceptional projects. Covers research costs (research assistants, datasets, LLM subscriptions, travel to present), not salary or overhead.

Research grants for academic scholars studying how AI is changing jobs, productivity and economic opportunity. Economics-leaning; IHS is a libertarian-leaning institute. Funds direct research costs only. No country restriction stated. Deadline 15 December 2026 (no time zone given).

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: BlueDot Impact: Seed Grants for new AI safety and biosecurity projects (USD 20,000 to 200,000, rolling)
item.description:
BlueDot Impact
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: USD 20,000 to 200,000 for 6 to 12 months (requests under USD 20,000 go to BlueDot Rapid Grants). No application fee.

BlueDot Impact's Seed Grants fund the first 6 to 12 months of a new AI safety or biosecurity project or organisation, covering founders' living costs, compute, tools and running costs, and travel. WHAT YOU GET: USD 20,000 to 200,000 (smaller requests go to Rapid Grants).

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Outrider AI + Nuclear Reporting Fund (rolling)
item.description:
Outrider Foundation
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: Up to USD 10,000 per reporting project.

Outrider funds journalists and outlets reporting on the intersection of artificial intelligence and nuclear weapons: how AI is changing nuclear risk, command and control, and policy. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis through the Google Form linked from the fund page. No application fee.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Pantheon: Research Fellowship in robot learning (remote, USD 6,000/month) (rolling)
item.description:
Pantheon
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: USD 6,000 per month stipend (about USD 12,000 to 18,000 over the fellowship) plus enterprise-level compute for experiments. No application fee.

Pantheon, which builds general-purpose robot models, runs a remote research fellowship in which each fellow leads a project on an open problem the team meets while training and evaluating its models; strong results are folded into the next generation of those models.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Inciter Art (Fractured Atlas): quarterly open call for essays, 'tending to the hearth' (USD 750 stipend)
item.description: Fractured Atlas (Inciter Art) · deadline 02 Nov 2026 · USD 750 stipend per selected writer, paid by ACH deposit or check once the first draft is finished (a W-9 form is required). No submission fee.
